paper_title: Text Generation with Diffusion Language Models A Pre-training Approach   with Continuous Paragraph Denoise
caption: Effect of different diffusion steps on text generation quality, on XSum. The result is the optimal value of 5 Gaussian samples.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effect of varying diffusion steps on text generation quality, measured using ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L scores, on the XSum dataset. The horizontal axis, labeled "Diffusion Step," displays discrete values at 100, 250, 500, 1000, and 2000, representing different numbers of diffusion steps. The vertical axis represents the ROUGE scores, with values ranging from approximately 0 to 42, though no explicit scale or unit label is provided. For each diffusion step, three grouped bars correspond to the three ROUGE metrics: ROUGE-1 (blue with diagonal stripes), ROUGE-2 (green with dots), and ROUGE-L (orange with no pattern), as indicated in the legend. At 100 steps, the scores are 6.3 (ROUGE-1), 0.1 (ROUGE-2), and 3.0 (ROUGE-L). At 250 steps, they are 11.6, 0.4, and 8.3, respectively. At 500 steps, the scores increase to 21.1, 4.1, and 15.9. At 1000 steps, the values are 38.3, 16.5, and 30.7. At 2000 steps, the scores reach 41.2 (ROUGE-1), 19.1 (ROUGE-2), and 33.4 (ROUGE-L). All three ROUGE metrics show a general increasing trend with higher diffusion steps, with ROUGE-1 consistently achieving the highest scores, followed by ROUGE-L and then ROUGE-2. The bars are arranged in groups by diffusion step, with each group containing three bars in the same order as the legend. The chart does not include error bars or confidence intervals, and all values are explicitly labeled on top of each bar.
